A patient with a MAINZ I pouch reports weeks of progressive catheterization difficulty (indicating channel stenosis), followed by complete drainage failure, oliguria, severe lower abdominal pain, and dyspnea with cardiopulmonary decompensation. CT with retrograde pouch contrast demonstrates a large left laterodorsal reservoir wall defect with contrast extravasation into the peritoneum and free intraperitoneal fluid. Elevated WBC (15.3) and markedly elevated lactate (4.7 mmol/L) confirm systemic inflammatory response/sepsis from urinary peritonitis. The mechanism is: channel stenosis → outflow obstruction → pouch overdistension → wall rupture → intraperitoneal urine leak → chemical/bacterial peritonitis → sepsis and abdominal compartment physiology causing respiratory compromise. This is a well-described but rare complication of continent urinary diversions, particularly when catheterizable channels narrow over time.
